hero.filename: USS Radford (DD-446) steaming into Tulagi Harbour with 468 survivors form USS Helena (CL-50) on 6 July 1943.jpg
hero.caption: The U.S. Navy destroyer USS Radford (DD-446) steaming into Tulagi Harbour in the Solomons with a deckload of survivors of the sunken light cruiser USS Helena (CL-50), and with the wounded filling all available space below, 6 July 1943. Helena was sunk during the Battle of Kula Gulf the night before. Radford received Presidential Unit Citation for the rescue of 468 survivors.
hero.alt: The U.S. Navy destroyer USS Radford (DD-446) steaming into Tulagi Harbour in the Solomons with a deckload of survivors of the sunken light cruiser USS Helena (CL-50), and with the wounded filling all available space below, 6 July 1943. Helena was sunk during the Battle of Kula Gulf the night before. Radford received Presidential Unit Citation for the rescue of 468 survivors.

images.filename: USS Helena (CL-50) firing during the Battle of Kula Gulf, 6 July 1943 (80-G-54553).jpg
images.caption: Battle of Kula Gulf, 5-6 July 1943: The U.S. Navy light cruiser USS Helena (CL-50), in the center, firing during the Battle of Kula Gulf, just before she was torpedoed and sunk. The next ship astern is USS St. Louis (CL-49).

images.filename: Torpedo damage plan of USS Helena (CL-50) in the Battle of Kuly Gulf, 6 July 1943 (C l5001).jpg
images.caption: Torpedo damage of the U.S. Navy light cruiser USS Helena (CL-50) in the Battle of Kuly Gulf on 6 July 1943. The bow broke off after the first hit. Minutes later two torpedoes hit amidships after which the ship jacknifed.
images.alt: Torpedo damage of the U.S. Navy light cruiser USS Helena (CL-50) in the Battle of Kuly Gulf on 6 July 1943. The bow broke off after the first hit. Minutes later two torpedoes hit amidships after which the ship jacknifed.

images.filename: USS Helena (CL-50) survivors being greeted by Admiral Ainsworth, 7 July 1943.jpg
images.caption: Survivors of the U.S. Naval light cruiser USS Helena (CL-50) being greeted by Admiral Walden Ainsworth (with cap). Commander Charles L. Carpenter, senior officer of the first group of survivors rescued, is visible behind the Admiral.

images.caption: 80-G-54563:  Battle of the Kula Gulf, July 5-6, 1943.  Aboard USS Nicholas (DD 449), survivors of USS Helena (CL 50), which was torpedoed and sunk by the Japanese.  They are debarking at Espiritu Santo, New Hebrides, for a period of relaxation before shipping out for the battlefront again.   Photograph, July 1943.   Official U.S. Navy photograph, now in the collections of the National Archives.   (2016/07/19).

images.caption: 80-G-43403: Lieutenant Commander Warren C. Boles, USNR, who, after USS Helena (CL 50) was sunk in the Battle of Kula Gulf, helped to inspire a group of more than 50 survivors and lead them to Vella Lavella Island from which they were rescued.   Received September 20, 1943.    U.S. Navy photograph, now in the collections of the National Archives.  (2017/02/28).
